notes: This 18-page PDF combines all four Abfuhrbezirke (1-4, for Restabfall/Bio/Papier/Gelb/Grünschnitt/Weihnachtsbäume) plus a separate two-value Schadstoffe system (Bezirk A/B) into one dense colour-coded grid on p1 (Jan-Jun) and p16 (Jul-Dec, file numbering) — too easy to misread a cell's district by colour, so I instead used the plain-text 'Abfuhrtermine 2026' pages that list every district's dates by name; the front matter (p1 footer) points to them as printed page 14, which the out/png set did not render (it stopped at file p16 of an 18-page PDF). I rendered PDF pages 17 and 18 myself with PyMuPDF get_pixmap (an image render, not text extraction) into the scratch folder and read the dates from those images, same as any other tile. Picked 'Bezirk 1' (first/lowest numeric district) and 'Bezirk A' (first lettered district for Schadstoffe) per the tie-break rule. Bezirk 1 also has a second, parallel 'Restabfall (wöchentlich)' weekly track with its own different dates (e.g. Jan 2/15/29) — a different collection frequency for the same numbered district, presumably for a different property type on the same street grid; I used only the 'Restabfall (14-tägig)' column, listed first on the page, for 'rest', and left the weekly track out entirely rather than mixing two schedules under one bin key. 'Weihnachtsbäume' (Christmas-tree collection) is counted under gruen per the label key's 'Christbaum'; its Jan 19 'Alle Bezirke' catch-up date is included alongside Bezirk 1&4's Jan 9 date. 'Elektrogroßgeräte' has no matching key and was left out entirely. September has no Grünschnitt row for any district. Bio is weekly during September for Bezirk 1 (7/14/21/28), same seasonal step-up seen in the other two labelled calendars. Dates come from clean typeset text rather than a scan, and I spot-checked several against the weekday letters printed on the p1/p16 grid pages (which show the same year's dates independent of district) with no mismatches.
